Best framing: N30 handles Bangar town ↔ resort gateway; traditional longboat preserved for the experiential upper-river leg.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II is the right platform for BSB↔Bangar (18 nm cross-bay) and Empire↔Bangar (15 nm) — sheltered Brunei Bay, premium silent-arrival positioning. The N35 shallow-draft (18") variant matters for Bangar ↔ Ulu Ulu Resort lower-river access; the upper rainforest river stays with traditional longboats by design.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR not particularly relevant here — all Temburong corridors fit inside Pioneer II range. Quanta-LR potentially extends to a future Temburong↔Limbang cross-border eco-corridor if Sarawak partnership emerges.

regulatory_note: Brunei Forestry Department governs Ulu Temburong NP access; visitor cap is sultan-endorsed conservation policy. BMPA governs water transit. Cross-border to Limbang Sarawak requires Malaysian licensing. Sultan-endorsed eco-luxury framing eases all approvals — this is precisely the niche the Brunei Tourism Master Plan was designed around. NO direct palace outreach; route through Brunei Tourism Board. Flag `hold_authority: pending_intro` for any royal-household engagement.
seasonality: Year-round rainforest tropical (26-32°C; humid). November-February heavier rainfall; Temburong River water levels affect upper-river longboat operations more than lower-river N30 ops. Visitor flow peaks Aug-Oct (Brunei dry season + school holidays) and Jul-Aug Sultan's Birthday period.

summary: Temburong is Brunei's eastern enclave — physically separated from the rest of the country by Malaysian Limbang (Sarawak), and home to Ulu Temburong National Park, one of Southeast Asia's most intact primary rainforest reserves. Historically, the ONLY practical way to reach Bangar (the district capital) from BSB was a 45-min river-and-bay speedboat through Brunei Bay. The Sultan Haji Omar Ali Saifuddien Bridge (opened March 2020, 30 km, longest in SE Asia) created a road option — ~30 min by car — and rerouted most local traffic. But the Ulu Temburong eco-luxury circuit (Ulu Ulu Resort, canopy walkway, longhouse experiences) still uses river-boats from Bangar deep into the protected park interior, where roads are intentionally absent.
tagline: Brunei's "Green Jewel" — a primary-rainforest enclave reached historically by river boats; the 2020 Temburong Bridge changed road access but did NOT replace the eco-luxury water approach.
